  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Eric Woods (E019) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires the role to own the system, which does not apply here. Requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: IT DB confirms Eric Woods (E019) is an Engineer. He is full-time and requests write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires the role to own the system (Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Engineer). Requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 3 (ticket 1):

  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Finance DB confirms Eric Woods (E019) is an Engineer and full-time. Requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires the role to own the system (Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Engineer). Requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 4 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Compliance DB confirms Eric Woods (E019) is an Engineer, full-time. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not Engineer, so admin is not permitted. Full-time employees may have up to write; requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 5 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Facilities DB confirms Eric Woods (E019) is an Engineer. Full-time employee requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires the role to own the system (Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Engineer). Requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 6 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Eric Woods (E019) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. He has basic training, so maximum is read. Requested write exceeds policy, so recommend read.
reason: Eric Woods (E019) requests write access to Payroll. Most notes (HR/IT/Finance/Compliance/Facilities) indicate he is a full-time Engineer, which would permit write. However, the Security DB note directly contradicts this, stating he is a contractor with basic security training. Under the access policy, contractors may only have read without advanced security training, and never admin; with basic training his maximum is read. Because the requested level (write) exceeds the maximum permitted for a contractor with basic training, and given the direct conflict in evidence, I apply the more restrictive/least-privilege interpretation supported by the Security DB. Granting read (the maximum allowed) rather than write.
